claims.claim: Microsoft Xbox One S All-Digital Edition Console (Disc-free)
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a disc drive slot visible on the front of the console.
The unit is covered in clear plastic film which can hide scratches or scuffs.
Internal inspection or high-resolution photos of warranty seals are required.
Requires a stress test under load which cannot be confirmed via photos.
The condition of the rear ports is not shown in the report.
Game controllers are listed as not shown in the witness report.
The receipt is not shown in the photos.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be mechanicaly failed or unable to read discs.
risks.proof: A video clip showing a disc being inserted, recognized by the system, and ejected.
risks.if_unproven: As a digital-only unit (matching the seller's lower-spec claim).

risks.risk: The console may be banned from Xbox Network/Live services.
risks.proof: A video showing the console successfully logged into a profile and accessing the Xbox Store.

risks.risk: The internal storage may be the minimum capacity (500GB).
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'Storage' section in the system settings.

risks.risk: The promised controllers (pads) may be missing, third-party, or have 'stick drift'.
risks.proof: A photo of the controllers and a video showing them navigating the menu.
risks.if_unproven: As a console-only listing without accessories.

proof_requests: Video of the console booting up and reading a physical game disc.
Photo of the controllers and the UK receipt mentioned.
Screenshot of the 'System Information' or 'Storage' settings page.
Video showing the console connecting to the internet and the Xbox Store.
response.reason: The witness identifies the item as an Xbox One S with a disc drive, which contradicts the seller's 'All-Digital' claim. It is priced as a base 500GB unit with a non-functional disc drive and no controllers.
